nodes.norm_label: note: run this test from the hack/boilerplate directory. $ python -m unittest...

nodes.label: Dex issuers dex-a / dex-b
nodes.rationale: Each Dex issuer: value is set to exactly its Service DNS URL so the discovery document's iss matches what the proxy dials; serving cert SANs cover the in-cluster Service DNS.

nodes.label: Multi-issuer demo flow (two Dex issuers, one proxy)
nodes.norm_label: multi-issuer demo flow (two dex issuers, one proxy)
nodes.rationale: Proves the headline feature locally: a single proxy trusting two independent OIDC issuers, with tokens from either impersonated as distinct users (oidc-a:alice, oidc-b:bob). Runs in kind with no cloud accounts, DNS, or browser.

nodes.label: Auth -> impersonate -> audit -> proxy handler chain
nodes.norm_label: auth -> impersonate -> audit -> proxy handler chain
nodes.rationale: Every request passes the same pipeline: authenticate (with TokenReview fallback), resolve impersonation target (SubjectAccessReview, header cap 431), impersonate as own ServiceAccount recording originaluser.jetstack.io-* extras, then stream to API server. Each stage maps to a handler in pkg/proxy.

nodes.label: Request flow (kubectl -> proxy -> JWKS -> apiserver -> RBAC)
nodes.norm_label: request flow (kubectl -> proxy -> jwks -> apiserver -> rbac)
nodes.rationale: Proxy performs authentication itself so OIDC login works without touching the API server's --oidc-* flags, which are unreachable on managed control planes (EKS, GKE, AKS).

nodes.label: HTTP 431 Request Header Fields Too Large rejection
nodes.norm_label: http 431 request header fields too large rejection

nodes.label: --allow-reserved-groups
nodes.rationale: Only listed system: groups are permitted; there is no way to permit a reserved username because system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<name> is the most direct path to another identity's privileges. Entries must start with system: or startup is refused, since an unreserved entry is almost certainly a typo.

nodes.label: Kubernetes-style auditing options
nodes.rationale: Same auditing options as kube-apiserver except --audit-dynamic-configuration is not supported.

nodes.label: Impersonation model
nodes.rationale: Proxy authenticates as its own ServiceAccount and attaches Impersonate-* headers; impersonation replaces but does not bypass RBAC.

nodes.label: Inbound impersonation (kubectl --as)
nodes.rationale: Inbound Impersonate-* headers are honoured only after a SubjectAccessReview confirms the authenticated user may assume that identity.

nodes.label: OIDC issuer mutual TLS client cert/key flags
nodes.norm_label: oidc issuer mutual tls client cert/key flags
nodes.rationale: Apply to every issuer in both modes; file-backed credentials are re-read by client-go so rotation via the projected Secret (oidc.tlsClient.existingSecret) needs no pod restart.

nodes.label: originaluser.jetstack.io-* audit extra headers
nodes.rationale: Runtime API contract left unchanged from upstream so the API server audit log records who really made the request; extras are subresources requiring explicit impersonate RBAC.

nodes.label: --subject-access-review-timeout shared budget
nodes.rationale: A single shared budget across all SAR calls for one request, not per-call; must be greater than 0.

nodes.label: Token passthrough (--token-passthrough)
nodes.rationale: Alpha: tokens failing OIDC validation are tried via TokenReview and, if valid, forwarded as-is with no impersonation; --token-passthrough-audiences overrides the audience set.

nodes.label: Choose an authentication mode (single vs multi-issuer)
nodes.norm_label: choose an authentication mode (single vs multi-issuer)
nodes.rationale: When authenticationConfig.content is set the chart passes --authentication-config and omits issuer-specific --oidc-* flags; setting both fails startup.

nodes.label: kubectl kubeconfig with kubelogin exec plugin
nodes.norm_label: kubectl kubeconfig with kubelogin exec plugin

nodes.label: Serving TLS options (self-signed, cert-manager, own Secret)
nodes.norm_label: serving tls options (self-signed, cert-manager, own secret)

nodes.label: Structured AuthenticationConfiguration (apiserver.config.k8s.io v1/v1beta1)
nodes.rationale: Reuses the same file format kube-apiserver consumes since 1.30; useful on managed clusters where apiserver flags cannot change. Strictly validated at startup (unknown fields, duplicate issuers, invalid CEL rejected); only jwt: is supported, anonymous: rejected; read once at startup.

nodes.label: CEL claim mappings (username/groups expressions)
nodes.rationale: Groups expressions may return a list so one token can carry groups along several axes; prefixes must live inside expressions since prefix: only applies to claim:. Every referenced claim must be present or authentication fails; guard optional claims with has().

nodes.label: claimValidationRules
nodes.rationale: Pin org/owner IDs so a recycled name cannot inherit access; with expression-based usernames email_verified is not auto-enforced and must be checked explicitly.

nodes.label: Helm config checksum rolling restart
nodes.rationale: The config file is read once at startup, so the chart annotates the Deployment with a config checksum to trigger a rolling restart on change.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions issuer recipe
nodes.rationale: GitHub tokens carry no groups claim so CEL synthesizes one from repository_owner; newer sub embeds numeric IDs so decode a real token or use a CEL username.

nodes.label: GKE cluster ServiceAccount issuer recipe
nodes.rationale: Trusting the cluster's own issuer makes every ServiceAccount bindable without Google service accounts; one entry and prefix per source cluster makes system:serviceaccount subs collision-proof.

nodes.label: Internal issuer with private CA recipe
nodes.norm_label: internal issuer with private ca recipe
nodes.rationale: Systems you control should emit a real groups array so no CEL is needed and onboarding is a change in the issuing system, not cluster RBAC.

nodes.label: TeamCity (teamcity-oidc-jwt) issuer recipe
nodes.rationale: Raw sub is an internal ID chain; external-ID claims (build_type_external_id, project_external_id) make better identities.

nodes.label: make e2e hermetic end-to-end suite
nodes.rationale: Hermetic: builds images, creates its own kind cluster, runs test/e2e/suite, tears down on exit. Versions outside the manifest are refused; CI tests newest on PRs and the full window on the scheduled run.

nodes.label: Local multi-issuer test: kind and GitHub Actions token
nodes.norm_label: local multi-issuer test: kind and github actions token
nodes.rationale: GitHub only mints OIDC tokens inside a workflow run, so a mint workflow uploads the ~5 min token as an artifact which is downloaded via gh and used with kubectl --token against the proxy in kind.

nodes.label: AuSuccess / AuFail request log format
nodes.rationale: Every request is logged to stdout so a SIEM can ingest it; includes src, XFF, URI, inbound identity and outbound impersonated identity.

nodes.label: Security guidance (privileged component)
nodes.rationale: The proxy's ServiceAccount can impersonate users, groups and extras; keep hardened chart defaults, scope audiences and required claims, mind prefixes, use passthrough deliberately, know caching lag, configure trusted proxies.

nodes.label: Demo Helm values (proxy-values.yaml)
nodes.rationale: pullPolicy Never because the image is loaded into kind; readinessRequireAllIssuers true to prove multi-issuer initialization end to end.

nodes.label: demo/run.sh orchestration
nodes.rationale: Idempotent: builds the proxy image locally (chart default tag is not published for the fork), creates kind cluster, generates certs, deploys Dex, installs chart with --set-file authenticationConfig.content, applies RBAC, mints and verifies tokens.

nodes.label: C4 diagrams (c4/workspace.dsl, Structurizr)
nodes.rationale: Diagrams are generated from Structurizr DSL; edit the model and re-render rather than editing images by hand.

nodes.label: Caching and API-server protection
nodes.rationale: Passthrough TokenReview and inbound-impersonation SubjectAccessReview both scale with client behaviour; left unbounded they become API-server load. Caches follow the k8s.io/apiserver delegated auth precedent: 10s TTLs, definitive results only, 0 disables.

nodes.label: Configuration reference
nodes.rationale: Flags are defined in cmd/app/options/; --oidc-* flags mirror the kube-apiserver OIDC authenticator so single-issuer config carries over one-to-one.

nodes.label: .github/workflows/e2e-oidc-gha.yaml
nodes.rationale: Proves the union authenticator against the real GitHub Actions OIDC issuer alongside a local Dex issuer.

nodes.label: Dex password grant token minting
nodes.rationale: oauth2.passwordConnector: local + enablePasswordDB lets an ID token be minted with a single curl, avoiding a browser redirect; --resolve keeps SNI, certificate and iss consistent with the Service DNS name.

nodes.label: insecure-skip-tls-verify in the demo
nodes.rationale: Client-to-proxy TLS is skipped because the chart generates a self-signed serving cert in a local demo; this does not weaken the OIDC path since Dex certs are verified against the inlined CA and token signatures against JWKS.

nodes.label: Single-issuer vs multi-issuer mode mutual exclusivity
nodes.norm_label: single-issuer vs multi-issuer mode mutual exclusivity
nodes.rationale: When --authentication-config is set, issuer-specific --oidc-* flags are rejected; the OIDC TLS client cert/key pair is transport config shared by all issuers and therefore accepted in either mode.

nodes.label: --readiness-require-all-issuers readiness semantics
nodes.rationale: Default false: pod Ready once at least one issuer has fetched JWKS so a single IdP outage cannot block a rollout for every other system; pending issuers keep initializing in the background. true: Ready only when every issuer initialized. Configuration errors always fail startup.

nodes.label: Multi-issuer union authenticator
nodes.rationale: One authenticator per issuer combined into a union; a token is offered to each in turn and the first that accepts wins. Lets one proxy accept a corporate IdP and GitHub Actions OIDC simultaneously; per-issuer prefixes keep identities from colliding.

nodes.label: Bounded LRU caches (8192 entries)
nodes.rationale: Both caches are bounded so client-influenced input can never grow proxy memory without bound.

nodes.label: Errors never cached (fail-closed)
nodes.rationale: An unreachable API server or timed-out review fails only the request that saw it and is retried on the next; only definitive results are cached.

nodes.label: HMAC-SHA256 token cache keys
nodes.rationale: Tokens are never stored as keys; keys are HMAC-SHA256 with a per-instance random key over token and audiences, so keys cannot be precomputed and a memory dump does not yield tokens.

nodes.label: Impersonation header value cap (--max-impersonation-header-values)
nodes.rationale: Each impersonation header value costs one SubjectAccessReview and the count is client-controlled, so a cap (default 64), not a cache, is the right tool. kube-apiserver tolerates unbounded counts because its check is in-process; here every value is a network call. Counted the way the handler consumes them so case variants cannot bypass it.

nodes.label: Singleflight for concurrent SAR misses
nodes.rationale: Concurrent identical SAR misses share one review; if the shared call dies because another request was cancelled, waiters fall back to their own live check.

nodes.label: SubjectAccessReview decision cache
nodes.rationale: Split allow/deny TTLs tuned per failure mode: cached allow delays revocation, cached deny delays new grants. Key is the whole serialized SubjectAccessReviewSpec including requester UID so principals never share a decision; specs over 10000 bytes are never cached; hits produce identical error types so errors.Is and 403 semantics are unchanged.

nodes.label: TokenReview result cache
nodes.rationale: Split success/failure TTLs (--token-passthrough-cache-success-ttl / -failure-ttl, 10s each). Concurrent misses deliberately each run their own review on the caller's context so the request timeout and cancellation apply; duplicate reviews are the accepted cost. A cached success outlives token revocation up to the success TTL.

nodes.label: Reserved system: identity refusal
nodes.rationale: Kubernetes does not guard system: on claim mappings and the chart grants impersonate without resourceNames, so by default the proxy refuses (403) any system:-prefixed username and any system: group other than system:authenticated. The check runs in the authentication handler before the SAR so a forged group cannot feed the authorization decision; identity is refused rather than silently stripped. Defense in depth: prefixes remain the primary control. SAR-authorized Impersonate-* targets are left alone to preserve break-glass.

nodes.label: Trusted proxies and client IP resolution (--trusted-proxies)
nodes.norm_label: trusted proxies and client ip resolution (--trusted-proxies)
nodes.rationale: Default trusts nothing: X-Forwarded-For is client-supplied and honouring it unconditionally would let any direct client forge its IP, poisoning audit logs and the Remote-Client-IP extra. XFF is walked only when the direct peer is inside a trusted CIDR; RFC 7239 Forwarded is not parsed.

nodes.label: Distinct per-issuer prefixes
nodes.rationale: All issuers feed the same RBAC namespace; without distinct prefixes issuer B could mint a sub or group colliding with an identity bound for issuer A. Never use unprefixed usernames in a multi-issuer setup.

nodes.label: ClusterRole template (impersonation RBAC)
nodes.rationale: Grants impersonate on users/groups/serviceaccounts (core) and on uids plus userextras in authentication.k8s.io, and create on tokenreviews. UID impersonation lives in authentication.k8s.io unlike users/groups which are core.

nodes.label: End-to-end UID impersonation (Impersonate-Uid)
nodes.rationale: Impersonate-Uid is forwarded, the impersonation check reviews uids in the authentication.k8s.io group, and the chart grants impersonate on uids and the originaluser.jetstack.io-uid extra; deployments mapping a uid claim need the new RBAC.

nodes.label: CI gates: unit tests, e2e, govulncheck, Helm checks
nodes.norm_label: ci gates: unit tests, e2e, govulncheck, helm checks

nodes.label: hack/cherry-pick-pull.sh
nodes.rationale: Fetches the PR patch from a hardcoded jetstack URL; when cherry-picking from TremoloSecurity the URL must be adjusted.

nodes.label: Go module rename to github.com/rafpe/kube-oidc-proxy
nodes.rationale: Upstream code still imports github.com/jetstack/kube-oidc-proxy, so cherry-picked Go changes must have import paths rewritten before they build.

nodes.label: originaluser.jetstack.io-* impersonation extra keys
nodes.rationale: These runtime extra keys are part of the impersonation API contract and must never be rewritten during the import-path reconciliation.

nodes.label: Private vulnerability reporting via GitHub advisories
nodes.norm_label: private vulnerability reporting via github advisories

nodes.label: Supply-chain pinning (Actions by SHA, images by digest)
nodes.norm_label: supply-chain pinning (actions by sha, images by digest)

nodes.label: Supported versions (>= 1.1.0, post-fork)
nodes.rationale: 1.1.0 is the point at which the project became an independent fork; pre-fork releases are unsupported.

nodes.label: Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct v1.4
nodes.norm_label: contributor covenant code of conduct v1.4

nodes.label: Fork independence model
nodes.rationale: The fork does not depend on upstream for its security posture; its own Dependabot and weekly govulncheck workflow are the primary signal, so vulnerabilities are surfaced even without repository activity and nobody waits for an upstream release.

nodes.label: govulncheck reachability gating over Scorecard presence
nodes.norm_label: govulncheck reachability gating over scorecard presence
nodes.rationale: Scorecard lists OSV advisories by dependency presence; the project gates on govulncheck, which reports by reachability. Code-Review, Maintained, Fuzzing and CII-Best-Practices findings are knowingly accepted (single maintainer, recent repo, no fuzz targets).

nodes.label: GHA_AUDIENCE Audience Matching
nodes.rationale: The minted token's audience MUST equal the AuthenticationConfiguration `audiences` entry; both are set to kube-oidc-proxy-kind-test.

nodes.label: e2e-oidc-gha workflow
nodes.rationale: Multi-issuer e2e against the REAL GitHub Actions OIDC issuer: mints a genuine GHA ID token in-job and proves the union authenticator accepts it alongside a local Dex issuer through a single AuthenticationConfiguration. Skips fork PRs because id-token: write is not granted to them. Keeps a push trigger (unlike e2e.yaml) because sub/ref/workflow_ref claims genuinely differ between push and pull_request and it has diverged in practice.

nodes.label: mint-oidc-token workflow
nodes.rationale: Manual ops helper: mints a GitHub Actions OIDC token for audience kube-oidc-proxy-kind-test and uploads it as a 1-day artifact for local multi-issuer testing.

nodes.label: Cosign keyless signing of chart and image
nodes.norm_label: cosign keyless signing of chart and image

nodes.label: oras push of Artifact Hub ownership metadata to GHCR
nodes.norm_label: oras push of artifact hub ownership metadata to ghcr

nodes.label: Helm install (OCI registry, local checkout, raw manifests)
nodes.norm_label: helm install (oci registry, local checkout, raw manifests)

nodes.label: PR Release Metadata required check
nodes.rationale: Enforces the label/fragment relationship; the generated release PR is exempt only when repository, branch and autorelease: pending label all match.

nodes.label: Prepare Release workflow (release/next -> main)
nodes.rationale: Manual, serialized; computes next version, batches fragments, opens release PR with autorelease: pending. Refuses to run without that label because such a PR could never be published; requires Actions permission to open PRs.

nodes.label: release/major|minor|patch|skip PR labels
nodes.rationale: Highest label since the previous release wins (major > minor > patch); only-skip changes produce no release.

nodes.label: Release workflow (tag, publish image/chart, GitHub Release)
nodes.norm_label: release workflow (tag, publish image/chart, github release)
nodes.rationale: Merging the release PR is the human publication approval; verification (make verify test, all E2E shards) runs against the exact merge commit before a tag exists; then annotated immutable tag, signed image and chart, draft GitHub Release made public.

nodes.label: Publishing on Artifact Hub
nodes.rationale: Listing on Artifact Hub makes the chart discoverable beyond GitHub and surfaces the cosign signature already attached to every release.

nodes.label: Unified release workflow TDD evidence
nodes.rationale: RED/GREEN evidence: contract check failed on missing pr-release-metadata.yml then passed; actionlint and go test pass; reusable E2E receives target_ref. make verify test blocked by missing boilerplate headers in demo/run.sh and demo/cleanup.sh.

nodes.label: Release recovery: never move a tag, fix forward
nodes.norm_label: release recovery: never move a tag, fix forward
nodes.rationale: If publication fails after tag creation, dispatch Release with the existing tag; it verifies the tag belongs to main, reruns checks and E2E, and resumes publication, refusing to move a tag or overwrite a published release.

nodes.label: review:claude job
nodes.rationale: Runs anthropics/claude-code-action with a threat-model prompt (auth bypass, impersonation/header smuggling, TokenReview/SubjectAccessReview caching, audit coverage, fail-open paths) and a JSON schema output {approve, summary}. Auto-approval only when approve==true AND the PR is not cross-repository.

nodes.label: review:release-approve job
nodes.rationale: Checks out .github/scripts from main (not the PR merge ref) so approval guards cannot be rewritten from release/next itself. Uses RELEASE_APPROVE_PAT because github-actions[bot] authors the release PR and cannot approve its own PR. Serialized via concurrency group release-approve so overlapping pull_request/workflow_run triggers see each other's review.

nodes.label: release/* PR Labels
nodes.rationale: Every ordinary PR merged to main carries exactly one of release/major, release/minor, release/patch, release/skip. The label decides the semver bump and the changelog category; release/skip means no version or changelog impact.

nodes.label: Changelog Fragment (.changes/unreleased/*.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Per-PR YAML with kind and body fields; batched by Prepare Release into a CHANGELOG.md section and deleted, and release.yaml refuses to tag while any unbatched fragment remains.

nodes.label: autorelease: pending Label
nodes.rationale: Marks the generated release PR; exempts it from release/* label checks, lets Claude Review auto-approve it, and is required by release.yaml's verify guard. Never created by automation; see docs/releases.md repository setup.

nodes.label: release/next Branch
nodes.rationale: Bot-owned branch holding the generated release commit; must originate from the same repository and is the only head ref that can trigger Release.

nodes.label: Pull Request Template
nodes.rationale: Checklist mirrors CI gates: go test ./cmd/... ./pkg/..., make e2e on behaviour change, exactly one release/* label, and a .changes/unreleased fragment for non-skip changes.

nodes.label: Release Drafter Config
nodes.rationale: Version resolution is driven purely by release/major|minor|patch|skip PR labels (default patch). Prepare Release uses it only to calculate a version and draft notes; publication is gated exclusively by the generated release/next PR.

nodes.label: Claude Review workflow
nodes.rationale: Two paths: release PRs (autorelease label) are approved without review after the diff is verified to carry only generated changelog/fragment changes; '@claude review' comments by the OWNER trigger a Claude code review that approves only on a clean verdict. Listens to workflow_run of Prepare Release as a belt-and-braces trigger in case GitHub suppresses GITHUB_TOKEN pull_request events again; the approve step is idempotent.

nodes.label: PR Release Metadata workflow
nodes.rationale: Enforces the metadata Prepare Release consumes: exactly one release/* label; each .changes/unreleased/*.yaml fragment has a kind in {Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security, Dependencies} and a non-empty body; release/skip PRs must add no fragments, non-skip PRs must add at least one. The generated release/next PR with 'autorelease: pending' is exempt.

nodes.label: Prepare Release workflow
nodes.rationale: Manual dispatch: release-drafter computes the next version and a draft release; fragments are batched into CHANGELOG.md under the <!-- next-release --> marker, committed to release/next (force-pushed) and a PR titled 'chore: release vX.Y.Z' with label 'autorelease: pending' is opened or updated. Verifies the label exists read-only BEFORE pushing because gh resolves labels before creating the PR, and branches on PR existence rather than `create || edit` so the create's real error is not swallowed.

nodes.label: Untrusted PR Content / Fork No-Auto-Approve Guard
nodes.norm_label: untrusted pr content / fork no-auto-approve guard
nodes.rationale: PR diff, description, commits and comments are treated as untrusted data; any text attempting to steer the verdict is itself a blocking finding. Fork PRs get a review but never an auto-approval so a prompt-injected verdict cannot become a counted review.

nodes.label: release-image chart job
nodes.rationale: Packages chart with version == appVersion == release, pins the Artifact Hub image annotation in Chart.yaml to the release, pushes to oci://ghcr.io/<owner>/charts and signs by digest. cosign logs in to GHCR explicitly because `helm registry login` does not populate the docker config it reads.

nodes.label: build workflow
nodes.rationale: Publishes a mutable development image (:edge and :main-<sha>) to GHCR on every push to main so unreleased changes can be tested. Versioned immutable images are release-image.yaml's job. Concurrency never cancels in progress so a pushed :edge image is always fully signed with its SBOM.

nodes.label: helm-chart workflow
nodes.rationale: Path-filtered to chart/kube-oidc-proxy/** and itself; runs helm lint and helm template against the single-issuer and multi-issuer CI value fixtures.

nodes.label: release-image workflow
nodes.rationale: Builds and publishes the versioned image (:X.Y.Z and :latest) and the OCI Helm chart for a release tag. Triggered by release.yaml via workflow_call, by manual tag pushes, or by workflow_dispatch backfill. A tag pushed by github-actions[bot] is release.yaml's own push, already covered by workflow_call, so the job guard skips it to prevent double publish (GitHub now DOES fire workflow triggers from GITHUB_TOKEN events, observed 2026-09-01).

nodes.label: Cosign Keyless Signing and SBOM Attachment
nodes.norm_label: cosign keyless signing and sbom attachment
nodes.rationale: Images are signed by digest with cosign keyless (id-token: write) and an SPDX SBOM from anchore/sbom-action is attached; SBOM steps are continue-on-error so a supply-chain metadata failure never blocks the image publish. Same pattern reused for dev (:edge) and release images and for the OCI Helm chart.

nodes.label: lint:go job
nodes.rationale: golangci-lint v2.12.2 with only-new-issues: true and PR-only trigger: the repo carries pre-existing findings being retired incrementally, so the linter gates on issues introduced by the PR rather than blocking on legacy debt.

nodes.label: pkg/mocks/authenticator.go (generated Token mock)
nodes.rationale: Generated in CI (not committed) by go.uber.org/mock/mockgen for the k8s.io/apiserver authenticator.Token interface; test.yaml, its lint job and fuzz.yaml all regenerate it before building.

nodes.label: fuzz workflow
nodes.rationale: Go native fuzzing for parsers on attacker-controlled input, run weekly (Wednesday 05:42 UTC) or on dispatch rather than per-PR so a merge never gates on a nondeterministic search; seed corpora already run in test.yaml. Inputs pass through env, not ${{ }} interpolation, so a dispatch value cannot be spliced into the command line. Failing corpus uploaded so the crasher can be committed as a regression seed.

nodes.label: test workflow
nodes.rationale: Build, unit tests, vet, gofmt and lint gate for PRs and pushes to main; e2e lives in e2e.yaml. Cancels superseded PR runs but never runs on main.

nodes.label: golangci-lint Config
nodes.rationale: Schema v2; defaults (errcheck, govet, ineffassign, staticcheck, unused) plus bodyclose, gosec, revive (dot-imports) requested in issue #60. staticcheck ST1000 is excluded because every file opens with the Jetstack copyright header rather than a 'Package X' doc comment (house style, not a defect). Test files and test/ get lighter treatment (no bodyclose/errcheck/gosec; revive and ST1001 allowed for Ginkgo/Gomega dot-imports); hack/ skips revive. Formatters: gofmt, goimports.

nodes.label: --allow-reserved-groups (replaces --allow-reserved-identity-claims)
nodes.rationale: Permits named system:-prefixed groups instead of disabling the reserved-identity guard wholesale; reserved usernames can never be permitted. The replaced flag never appeared in a release.

nodes.label: --max-impersonation-header-values cap (HTTP 431)
nodes.rationale: Every Impersonate-* header value fans out into a SubjectAccessReview, so an unbounded header set lets a client generate unbounded authorization load; capping at 64 by default and rejecting with 431 before any SAR bounds the per-request cost.

nodes.label: SubjectAccessReview decision cache (allow/deny TTLs)
nodes.rationale: Bounded in-memory cache with separate allow and deny TTLs (default 10s, 0 disables) shields the API server from repeated reviews; trade-off is that revoking or granting an RBAC impersonation permission can take up to the TTL to be enforced.

nodes.label: TokenReview result cache (success/failure TTLs)
nodes.rationale: Caches TokenReview results (default 10s, matching the kube-apiserver delegated-auth cache) so repeated passthrough tokens do not each hit the API server; a revoked token can keep passing for up to the success TTL and a newly valid token can be rejected for up to the failure TTL. API-server errors are never cached.

nodes.label: Token passthrough
nodes.rationale: Non-OIDC bearer tokens (e.g. service-account tokens) are still usable through the proxy by validating them against the API server via TokenReview instead of rejecting them.

nodes.label: Reserved system: identity guard
nodes.rationale: An OIDC issuer must not be able to mint system:masters or a service-account username through the proxy's blanket impersonation rights. The check runs before the inbound-impersonation SubjectAccessReview and the 403 is audited against the presented identity; system:authenticated stays permitted because the proxy adds it itself.

nodes.label: test:e2e aggregator job
nodes.rationale: Branch protection requires a check literally named "test:e2e" (display name, not job id). Per-version/shard checks carry suffixes and can never satisfy it, so this always()-running aggregator is green only when every shard of every version succeeded; the versions job result is checked explicitly rather than trusting skip propagation.

nodes.label: test:e2e @ <version> job
nodes.rationale: One caller leg per Kubernetes version; a `uses:` job cannot carry timeout-minutes, so the called shard workflow bounds itself (45 min per shard).

nodes.label: test:e2e:versions job
nodes.rationale: Reads test/e2e/versions/kubernetes-versions.json at the same resolved ref as the shards so the matrix can never drift ahead of what the code declares. Guards: supported list non-empty, sorted newest-first (release path runs supported[0]).

nodes.label: test:unit job
nodes.rationale: Generates the Token authenticator mock with mockgen, checks gofmt, go build, go vet, runs go test for ./cmd/... ./pkg/... ./test/tools/... ./test/e2e/versions/... (packages needing no cluster), and runs make verify-e2e-shards so no Ginkgo case is unlabelled.

nodes.label: Kubernetes Version Matrix from Manifest
nodes.rationale: The committed manifest travels with the commit under test; the suite resolves each version to its digest-pinned kind node image through the same manifest. The proxy runs on clusters across the whole supported window (1.36/1.35 in production) so a PR must prove all of it.

nodes.label: Ginkgo Shard Label Partitioning
nodes.rationale: Suite is split by Ginkgo Label("shard-a"|"shard-b"|"shard-c") on framework.CasesDescribe containers: shard-a = impersonation, headers, probe; shard-b = authconfig, upgrade, audit; shard-c = passthrough, token, rbac, reserved identity. Each shard stands up its own kind cluster so wall-clock is the slowest shard, not the sum. hack/verify-e2e-shards.sh prevents an unlabelled case from silently running in no shard.

nodes.label: e2e workflow
nodes.rationale: Deliberately has NO push-to-main trigger: the pull_request run already tests the merge commit and release.yaml re-runs the suite at the release SHA, so a post-merge run was a third execution that across 200 runs caught nothing (10 runs, 0 failures). A twice-daily schedule (06:00/18:00 UTC) keeps drift detection at fixed cost. Full version matrix on pull_request/schedule/workflow_dispatch; newest-only under workflow_call from release.yaml (github.event_name is the caller's event, never 'workflow_call').

nodes.label: e2e-shards workflow
nodes.rationale: Reusable (workflow_call only) shard half of the e2e suite so e2e.yaml can call it once per Kubernetes version and the Actions UI shows a collapsible group per version. Installs kubectl matching the cluster version because the runner's kubectl tracks newest Kubernetes and would be outside the +/-1 minor skew for older matrix legs. Artifact names include shard and k8s version because upload-artifact v7 rejects duplicates.

nodes.label: Core API group (/api) audit RequestInfo classification fix
nodes.norm_label: core api group (/api) audit requestinfo classification fix
nodes.rationale: The audit server config named no legacy API prefix, so every /api request was recorded as a non-resource request with the HTTP method as verb and no objectRef; long-running and watch detection could never trigger. Events now carry the Kubernetes verb and objectRef.

nodes.label: Audit streaming requests as long-running (ResponseStarted)
nodes.rationale: exec, attach, portforward, log and proxy are recorded when the response starts, so a long session is not missing from the audit log while it runs or lost entirely if the proxy dies; cost is higher audit volume for those verbs.

nodes.label: Readiness reports not-ready until the proxy is serving
nodes.norm_label: readiness reports not-ready until the proxy is serving
nodes.rationale: Previously the readiness server started before the proxy handler chain, so a pod could join its Service while proxy-port requests could only queue.

nodes.label: OIDC token validation failures logged at -v=2 with remote address
nodes.norm_label: oidc token validation failures logged at -v=2 with remote address
nodes.rationale: An error from the bearer-token authenticator always means a token was present and failed, so at -v=5 it was invisible at any verbosity operators actually run.

nodes.norm_label: configurable readiness (first issuer vs all issuers)

nodes.label: Multi-issuer OIDC authentication
nodes.rationale: Headline fork feature: one proxy accepts tokens from several issuers via a Kubernetes AuthenticationConfiguration, each with its own audiences and claim prefixes, so a single deployment serves multiple identity providers.

nodes.label: release:publish job
nodes.rationale: Requires the GitHub release for the tag to already exist as a draft (staged by release-drafter in Prepare Release) and flips it to published; refuses if it is not a draft.

nodes.label: release:tag job
nodes.rationale: Immutable tag: if the tag already exists it must point at the verified SHA, otherwise fail; else create an annotated tag as github-actions[bot] and push.

nodes.label: release:verify job
nodes.rationale: Derives tag from PR title 'chore: release vX.Y.Z' (or dispatch input), requires strict semver, requires the SHA to be an ancestor of origin/main, CHANGELOG.md to contain the version heading, and no unbatched .changes/unreleased fragments; exports tag and sha outputs for every downstream job.

nodes.label: Release workflow
nodes.rationale: Fires when the release/next PR (same repo, label 'autorelease: pending') is merged, or by dispatch to recover an existing tag. Pipeline: verify -> check + e2e -> tag -> publish-artifacts (release-image) -> publish-release (undraft). Concurrency group 'release' never cancels.

nodes.label: Label-driven, review-gated release process
nodes.rationale: Ordinary merges never publish. Every PR carries exactly one release/* label and a changelog fragment; a maintainer runs Prepare Release, reviews the automation-owned release/next PR, and its merge triggers verification, sharded Kind E2E, an immutable tag, signed multi-arch images and the OCI chart.

nodes.label: Artifact Hub repository metadata (Verified Publisher)
nodes.rationale: Pushed once to the OCI registry (not per release) to claim ownership of the repository on Artifact Hub.

nodes.label: kube-oidc-proxy (project overview)
nodes.rationale: Managed clusters (EKS, GKE, AKS) do not expose the API server's --oidc-* flags, so a reverse proxy validates the bearer token and impersonates the user; existing RBAC stays authoritative.

nodes.label: Chart and image share one version
nodes.norm_label: chart and image share one version
nodes.rationale: On a tagged release the automation overrides both version and appVersion from the git tag; the committed values are only the development baseline.

nodes.label: Impersonation instead of credential sharing
nodes.rationale: The proxy forwards requests with its own ServiceAccount plus Impersonate-* headers so the API server evaluates RBAC for the mapped user; kubectl --as is gated by SubjectAccessReview so blanket impersonation rights are never handed to clients.

nodes.label: Supported Kubernetes window in PR e2e (1.37/1.36/1.35)
nodes.norm_label: supported kubernetes window in pr e2e (1.37/1.36/1.35)
nodes.rationale: PR e2e runs exercise the full supported window; the release path stays newest-only because the same code already passed the full window on its PR.

nodes.label: --trusted-proxies contract for audit sourceIPs
nodes.rationale: Forwarded headers from untrusted peers are stripped before auditing and before forwarding upstream so a client cannot spoof the audit trail via X-Forwarded-For; operators behind a load balancer must set --trusted-proxies to recover the real client IP.

nodes.label: Audit events for unauthenticated (401) requests
nodes.rationale: The unauthorized audit chain now initialises the audit context so failed authentication attempts leave a ResponseStarted event rather than no trace.

nodes.label: test/e2e/versions/kubernetes-versions.json (single source of truth)
nodes.rationale: Holds the current minor plus two prior with node images from one kind release; CI matrix, kind CLI version and local make e2e default derive from it. go test ./test/e2e/versions/ fails until manifest and go.mod agree so compatibility is verified, not assumed.

nodes.label: Dependabot Config
nodes.rationale: Weekly updates for gomod, github-actions and docker ecosystems; docker covers the root Dockerfile plus test/tools/issuer, test/tools/fake-apiserver and test/tools/audit-webhook because base images are pinned by digest and need refreshing.

nodes.label: codeql workflow
nodes.rationale: Go SAST via GitHub CodeQL (autobuild) on push to main, PRs and weekly Tuesday schedule; results feed the Security tab and satisfy the OpenSSF Scorecard SAST check.

nodes.label: scorecard workflow
nodes.rationale: OpenSSF Scorecard supply-chain analysis on push to main, weekly Monday schedule and branch_protection_rule changes (a Scorecard signal). publish_results: true feeds the README badge and public viewer; SARIF is uploaded to code scanning. persist-credentials: false on checkout.

nodes.label: security workflow
nodes.rationale: govulncheck ./... on push to main, PRs and weekly Monday 06:00 UTC so new advisories are caught even without repository activity.

nodes.label: Bug Report Issue Template
nodes.rationale: Collects version/image tag, Kubernetes provider, authentication mode (single-issuer --oidc-issuer-url vs multi-issuer --authentication-config) and redacted logs; explicitly redirects security vulnerabilities to SECURITY.md so they are never filed publicly.

nodes.label: Issue Template Config
nodes.rationale: Blank issues disabled; contact links route security reports to a private GitHub Security Advisory and general questions to docs/.

nodes.label: Deployment args: --authentication-config vs --oidc-* switch
nodes.rationale: Single branch on .Values.authenticationConfig.content selects the whole flag set; single-issuer values are injected via env vars sourced from the <fullname>-config Secret while the multi-issuer file is mounted from the same Secret at /etc/oidc/authentication-config.yaml.

nodes.label: checksum/config pod annotation (secret_config.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Hashing the rendered config Secret into a pod annotation forces a rollout whenever OIDC config changes.

nodes.label: Deployment volumes (config Secret, TLS Secret, client-TLS Secret)
nodes.norm_label: deployment volumes (config secret, tls secret, client-tls secret)

nodes.label: High-availability guidance (PDB + topology spread)
nodes.rationale: Ships single-replica; for production run 3 replicas with a PodDisruptionBudget and topologySpreadConstraints (preferred over anti-affinity), and keep readinessRequireAllIssuers false so one IdP outage cannot block a rollout.

nodes.label: values.authenticationConfig.content (multi-issuer)
nodes.rationale: Each issuer's CA must be inline under issuer.certificateAuthority because oidc.caPEM is ignored in this mode.

nodes.label: values.extraArgs / extraVolumes / extraVolumeMounts
nodes.rationale: Escape hatch for flags the chart does not model, e.g. audit-log-path and audit-policy-file with a mounted policy volume.

nodes.label: values.maxImpersonationHeaderValues
nodes.rationale: Caps INBOUND Impersonate-* headers from clients; distinct from extraImpersonationHeaders, which adds OUTBOUND extra user headers to forwarded requests.

nodes.label: values.oidc.tlsClient (issuer mTLS credentials)
nodes.rationale: Applies to every issuer in both modes; projected Secret updates are reloaded without restarting the proxy.

nodes.label: values.podDisruptionBudget
nodes.rationale: maxUnavailable takes precedence over minAvailable when set.

nodes.label: values.podSecurityContext (runAsNonRoot, runAsUser 1000, RuntimeDefault seccomp)
nodes.rationale: runAsUser is required because the image sets no USER, so runAsNonRoot alone would be rejected by admission.

nodes.label: values.readinessRequireAllIssuers
nodes.rationale: Default false: ready once at least one issuer has fetched JWKS, so a single IdP outage cannot block a rollout for all other systems.

nodes.label: values.securityContext (no privilege escalation, read-only rootfs, drop ALL)
nodes.norm_label: values.securitycontext (no privilege escalation, read-only rootfs, drop all)

nodes.label: CI fixture: multi-issuer values
nodes.rationale: Sets requiredClaims on purpose to prove it is ignored in multi-issuer mode, and tlsClient to prove shared OIDC transport credentials remain available.

nodes.label: CI fixture: single-issuer values
nodes.rationale: Exercises the --oidc-* flag path including the repeatable --oidc-required-claim flag.

nodes.label: Hardened SecurityContext by default
nodes.rationale: The proxy is a privileged component whose ServiceAccount can impersonate identities, so it runs non-root (uid 1000), read-only rootfs, all capabilities dropped, no privilege escalation, RuntimeDefault seccomp; relax readOnlyRootFilesystem only for local writes such as audit-log-path.

nodes.label: Mutually exclusive single-issuer / multi-issuer chart modes
nodes.norm_label: mutually exclusive single-issuer / multi-issuer chart modes
nodes.rationale: When authenticationConfig.content is non-empty the chart passes --authentication-config and omits issuer-specific --oidc-* flags; oidc.tlsClient stays available in either mode because its mTLS credentials apply to every issuer.
